hypotheses.statement: The base K is a number field and char(K) != 2.
Every Cayley-Dickson parameter a_i is a specified nonzero element of K.
A single multiplication, conjugation, norm, and sign convention for CD(K; a_1,...,a_n) is fixed.
For n=2, the selected construction is the quaternion central simple algebra to which the cited Hilbert-symbol criterion applies.
The local invariant certificate includes every relevant finite and infinite place and satisfies reciprocity.
For n=3, the norm form is the explicitly ordered three-fold Pfister form used by the cited local-global criterion.
Any n>=4 universal zero-divisor identity is valid for the chosen generalized doubling convention, arbitrary admitted nonzero parameters, and every admitted base field.
A split certificate supplies nonzero operands whose exact product is zero; any search-size bound is stated separately.
The integral octonion order, multiplication table, conjugation, and E8 norm identification are fixed exactly.
Each generator model states whether it is an integral similitude, real normalized map, triality triple, spin element, or projective reduction.
Every reduction prime avoids the discriminant and denominators of the selected integral model.
The finite target group, quadratic-form type, center quotient, and determinant/spinor-norm conditions are fixed.
The spectral operator records direction, inverse closure, generator multiplicity, and normalization.
The Hurwitz order, norm convention, shell definition, and parity restrictions on n are fixed.
The reduction map to matrices and the passage to the stated finite projective group are well-defined.
The unit action and the factor represented by the divisor 2 in the proposed intensity are derived rather than assumed.
The occupancy vector includes every target fiber, including zero multiplicities.
Any asymptotic specifies a joint sequence (n,ell), admissibility conditions, and the mode of convergence.
The discrepancy measure, test-function class, normalization, and finite target are fixed.
A source theorem with explicit constants is pinned and every source hypothesis is mapped to a verified local hypothesis.
All bad primes, local factors, conductors, levels, and numerical rounding directions are recorded.
A division algebra has no pair of nonzero elements with zero product.
A is an eight-dimensional real positive-definite composition algebra and N(xy)=N(x)N(y).
X and S are finite sets, r:X->S is a map, and m_s is the cardinality of the fiber r^{-1}(s).
A is the real division octonion algebra; x and y are nonzero, so x, y, and xy admit normalized left multiplications.
A finite group G acts on a finite set X and r:X->S is G-invariant.
C is an octonion composition algebra over a finite field F_q of odd characteristic; x and y have nonzero norm.
A is any algebra over a commutative ring and [x,y,z]=x(yz)-(xy)z.
The committed F3 multiplication tensor is interpreted with quadratic norm N(x)=sum_i x_i^2 and basis e0,...,e7.
F_q has odd characteristic not dividing n, n>=6, C is the split eight-dimensional octonion norm space with determinant square class 1, and Q_D,n is the normalized Descartes form.
